item.description:
Settings and menu

  • The menu-bar gear brings Settings to the foreground on the first click, including when its window is already open behind another application.
  • The Codex icon stays visible in light and dark appearance and follows the selected control's color.

Web search

  • Codex's managed profile enables live web search. Existing connections can adopt the setting with Apply; disconnecting restores the original search mode.
  • Web Search settings now use wording shared by all supported agents.

Compatibility

  • Requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 14 or later.
  • Existing routes and credentials are preserved.

Claude Auto compatibility

  • New Disabled thinking → Use low effort option in each provider's Advanced settings helps reasoning backends produce complete short classifier verdicts when Claude requests thinking to be disabled.
  • Existing effort choices, token limits and model decisions are preserved. The option is off by default and can be enabled only for providers that need it.
  • Claude Code no longer disables prompt caching in its connection profile.

Web search

  • Exa is now available alongside Firecrawl, Tavily and Brave, with configurable search limits, highlighted results and domain filters.

Updates

  • Homebrew updates now ship alongside the in-app updater, using the same verified release DMG.
  • Published versions are marked as the latest stable release so website downloads resolve to the current version.

Compatibility

  • Requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 14 or later.
  • Existing configuration, routes and credentials are preserved. The new provider option can be left at Pass through to keep the previous behavior.

Settings and menu

  • A consistent native design across all settings: shared section cards, aligned selectors, compact toolbar actions, lighter typography, and a dark main pane distinct from the sidebar.
  • Browse available models in collapsible provider cards with individual and group switches. Codex's model list no longer has a search field.
  • Overview, Claude and Codex share six usage metrics and a taller token-history chart. Inspect a day or return to the full thirty-day period; client tabs filter statistics and place their settings below them.
  • The menu gear opens Settings directly. About, Check for Updates and Quit are available at the bottom of every tab.
  • Refined model selection and Apply controls, reliable rendering on repeated menu openings, and appearance updates when macOS switches between light and dark mode.
  • Duplicate providers with independent identities and credentials, and review the consequences before deleting one.
  • Improved accessibility labels for toolbar actions, connection status and monitoring controls.

Monitoring

  • New Monitoring settings provide Prometheus/OpenMetrics metrics at /metrics and optional structured JSON logs at /logs, over local HTTP or HTTPS when available.
  • Export metrics and logs independently through OTLP/HTTP JSON, with separate destinations, Bearer authentication, delivery status and a synthetic Test export action.
  • Compact, collapsible export settings include preset intervals and complete HTTP/HTTPS addresses through Copy URL. A Prometheus and Loki Docker Compose lab is included for integration testing.
  • Monitoring logs contain controlled request metadata without prompts, response bodies or credentials. Export queues and retries are bounded in memory.
  • Provider errors reported inside successful HTTP streams are counted as failures without changing the response delivered to the client. Local log pages preserve timestamp precision and respect their byte limit.

Codex approval reviews

  • Choose an approval review model independently of the default task model, or use Same as default. Reviews use the selected provider's existing queue and concurrency limits.
  • Adjust the approval review model from Settings or the Codex menu tab. The internal review alias stays hidden from the task model catalog.
  • After upgrading, Apply the connected Codex profile to regenerate its managed catalog with approval routing.

Gateway and tools

  • Honor a client's refusal of external web search while keeping ordinary and namespaced client tools available.
  • Preserve supported completed tool history across provider switches, restore namespaces and support client-executed Responses tool discovery.
  • Validate tool output against the request's declared contract and reject unsupported provider-hosted execution.
  • Preserve incomplete and failed Responses when adapting client tools, and avoid starting a web search from an interrupted response.
  • Add GET and HEAD /api/hello for local connectivity checks.

Compatibility

  • Configuration upgrades to format 8. LittleSwitch 0.3.1 cannot read it. To downgrade, stop the app and restore a compatible pre-upgrade configuration. Original configurations are retained under Backups/Configuration/BeforeMigration, outside normal backup rotation. This protection applies when loading an older configuration after this fix; it cannot recreate a backup for an installation already upgraded to format 8.
  • Local /metrics is enabled by default. /logs and both OTLP exports remain disabled until enabled in Settings. /logs is a LittleSwitch read API; OTLP is the standard log export format.
  • /api/quota and its Z.ai quota integration are removed.
  • Adapted Responses requests require complete history in input; non-null previous_response_id and conversation references are rejected on those paths. Transparent native requests retain support for those references.
  • The former Logs settings page is removed. Internal diagnostic capture, retention and replay remain available.
  • Existing token history is preserved. When older data cannot establish a client's error or web-search counts, the metric is shown as unavailable.

Fixes

  • Web-search domain exclusions now hold on every client. A Codex or OpenCode request's blocked domains reached the model's searches unfiltered; the filter now maps to the provider's exclude list the way Claude requests already did.
  • Forcing a search no longer fails the turn. A Claude request pinning its tool choice to the built-in web search tool kept naming a tool the provider never sees after the gateway swaps in its own, and the provider rejected the whole request; the forced choice now follows the swap.

Breaking changes

  • The gateway is loopback-only. "Expose LittleSwitch to the network" is removed: the gateway binds 127.0.0.1 and the authority check accepts only loopback hosts. LAN clients stop connecting after this update. The loopback TLS identity — localhost and 127.0.0.1 under the private authority — cannot vouch for a LAN hostname, so network clients would fail certificate validation with no way to fix it from the app. Configurations carrying the old setting migrate silently to loopback-only.

Improvements

  • Claude route edits now wait for Apply. While Claude Desktop is connected, model remaps stage as a draft instead of reaching running conversations immediately. Apply commits them in one step — one save, one routing swap — and the menu and settings mark every application that holds unapplied changes, so a disconnect never discards edits unseen.
  • The Fable route. Fable 5 joins the route catalog alongside Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku, and Claude Code's managed settings learn it as a default model.
  • Brave joins the web-search providers. Brave Search sits next to Firecrawl and Tavily in Settings → Web Search: one API key (Search plan), up to 20 results per search, country filters honored. Search queries keep every character — including a literal plus — through to the provider.
  • Claude Code speaks https when the gateway anchor is trusted. The managed Claude Code origin follows the same trust state as the Claude Desktop profile: https while the loopback certificate is trusted, plain http otherwise, so a terminal session is never stranded on an origin it cannot validate.
  • The gateway's own endpoints moved to `/health` and `/api/` (about, web search). Clients still holding the previous `/_little_switch/` addresses keep working during a one-release transition window.
  • Testing a split-surface provider — a z.ai preset with the optional Anthropic URL — now probes model discovery at the base URL, so the connection test reflects what routing actually uses.

Improvements

  • **Claude Desktop web search through the gateway.** The Desktop's built-in web-search server now runs against LittleSwitch itself: searches execute on the configured provider (Firecrawl or Tavily), honor the results limit, appear in Logs, and need no credential in any configuration file.
  • **The gateway speaks https and plain http on one port.** Claude Desktop rides https — its managed web-search contract accepts nothing else — while Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode keep plain http with no client-side migration. The first inbound byte decides.
  • **The https identity is a private loopback authority.** Its signing key is created in memory, signs exactly one leaf, and is destroyed before issuance returns; the anchor macOS trusts can never vouch for anything new. One consent prompt on first connect, then silence — toggling the Claude switch never re-prompts. Renewal is automatic inside a 30-day margin of the 825-day validity.
  • The menu's usage block now shows the token direction — input, cached, output — in a two-row grid instead of one blended total.
  • Every published version of Claude's built-in web-search tool is bridged as a direct call, so a client that upgraded to `web_search_20260209` or later no longer loses whole conversations to an HTTP 400.

Fixes

  • A missing web-search provider key now answers 503 "Web search credential is missing" instead of a misleading provider failure, matching the earlier 401 diagnosis fix.
  • Idle TCP connections to the gateway no longer park a task forever; silent peers and oversized handshakes are closed at the decision bound.
  • Claude Desktop's profile only advertises the https origin once the trust anchor is actually installed, so a dismissed or failed consent prompt degrades to plain http instead of cutting the Desktop off entirely.

Improvements

  • Codex's model picker now shows readable model names — `z.ai/glm-4.6`, `ollama/qwen3.5:9b-mlx` — instead of opaque encoded identifiers, described by the product name alone.
  • z.ai providers: the OpenAI-compatible coding path is the base URL and the Anthropic path becomes an optional second surface, editable in the provider form ("Anthropic URL (optional)"). Messages and count-tokens ride the Anthropic URL when present; discovery and chat completions mount at the base URL.
  • The provider form leads with the connection test outcome rows.

Fixes

  • vLLM providers: streaming responses with `null` reasoning content or absent function-call fields no longer masquerade as stream failures.
  • The Responses wire resolves by automatic detection again; the z.ai base-URL heuristic is gone.

Improvements

  • Codex's model picker now shows readable model names — `z.ai/glm-4.6`, `ollama/qwen3.5:9b-mlx` — instead of opaque encoded identifiers, described by the product name alone.
  • z.ai providers: the OpenAI-compatible coding path is the base URL and the Anthropic path becomes an optional second surface, editable in the provider form ("Anthropic URL (optional)"). Messages and count-tokens ride the Anthropic URL when present; discovery and chat completions mount at the base URL.
  • The provider form leads with the connection test outcome rows.

Fixes

  • vLLM providers: streaming responses with `null` reasoning content or absent function-call fields no longer masquerade as stream failures.
  • The Responses wire resolves by automatic detection again; the z.ai base-URL heuristic is gone.

Fixes

  • When a provider's model discovery cannot reach the endpoint, the error now names the actual connection problem — "Read timeout", "Remote connection closed" — instead of an opaque `(AsyncHTTPClient.HTTPClientError error 1.)`, so script-authenticated providers show whether the endpoint, not the script, is the one failing.

Always-there brand marks

  • The menu's Claude Desktop and Codex rows now show LittleSwitch's own bundled brand marks instead of borrowing the installed applications' icons, so every row reads correctly from the very first launch — no matter which apps are installed.

Fixes

  • Provider save failures are now reported inside the editor sheet instead of a generic app alert.

Live model remaps — Claude Code & Claude Desktop

  • Remapping a route now applies immediately to running Claude apps: no relaunch, and open conversations follow along.
  • The served model catalog is invariant: route IDs and display names never move, so clients keep their model picker selections across remaps.
  • New Model indicator setting: choose how mapped routes are marked in the served model lists (⇌ equilibrium, ⇄ swap, ⇢ routed, ↦ maps-to, or plain).

Tabbed status menu

  • The menu is now organized into Overview, Claude, and Codex tabs.
  • The Claude tab maps the Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku routes in place with steppers and a single Apply action; the Codex tab sets the default Codex model.
  • Each tab shows its client's 30-day token history chart.
  • Steppers preview the chosen model immediately and reconcile when the apply lands.

Fixes

  • Codex refusals now explain which agents form was refused instead of surfacing a raw error code.
  • Compact token counts hold steady at display-rounding boundaries.
  • Menu tab content spacing is balanced top and bottom.
